$doc: Content and geometry for <PromiseWalk>, section 05. ONE LABEL PER STAGE, ONE OR MORE MEDIA UNDER IT. Every string a reader sees lives here; the component holds no copy and no numbers. Widths and floors come from this file's $retinaDoc, not from lib/bento-slots.json — the walk is not a bento and does not use slots.
$stageDoc: THE STAGE NAMES ARE JOURNEYLINE'S, VERBATIM, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM. Arrive / Browse / Decide / Purchase / Post purchase are the five stages the reader met in section 03, two sections earlier, on a line that ended angry. Reading them again here - same words, same order, now with a screen against each - is what makes this section the payoff rather than a gallery. Rename one here and it stops rhyming with the drawing; rename one there and this stops being recognisable. They move together or not at all. THE FRAME RULE, ADDED 31 Aug: EVERY DESKTOP-PAGE STAGE IS A CONTEXT FRAME THEN A DETAIL FRAME; THE TWO PHONE STAGES ARE SINGLE. Eight frames, five stages. That is a rule rather than a per-stage judgement, which is exactly what the set it replaced was missing - every asset in that one sat between the two jobs, too small to read and too partial to place. At a 660 cell a 1440px page renders at 46%, so 14px UI copy lands at 6.4px: NO CROP OF A WHOLE PAGE IS READABLE AT THIS SIZE and none should try to be. The context frame says where you are; the detail frame is the one you can read.
$spineDoc: THE LABEL COLUMN IS THE POINT, NOT A LAYOUT CONVENIENCE. Aligned left at one edge down the whole section, the five names form a vertical spine a skimmer reads as a sequence before looking at a single image. If the labels ragged, the spine is gone and the walk is a list of pictures. That is why every stage is two-column with no full-width exception, and why `align-items: start` pins each label to the top of its span rather than centring it.
$decideDoc: DECIDE HOLDS TWO MEDIA UNDER ONE LABEL, AND THE SHARING IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN COSMETIC. An earlier draft printed 'Decide' twice, once per screen. A vertical column of six labels with the same word in it twice reads as a mistake before it reads as a decision, and the spine's whole job is to be scannable as five stages. Sharing the cell makes the spine exactly five entries and says the true thing: one stage that took two screens to answer. Below 1024 the shared label sits above the first of its two figures and the second follows unlabelled — verified at 390 rather than assumed, because that is where it could orphan.
$retinaDoc: THE MEDIA CELL IS 660px, AND 380px FOR THE TWO PHONE STAGES. Both caps are retina decisions. 660 rather than 860: at 660 the floor is 1320 and every asset clears it, where at 860 the floor is 1720 and four of six fail - two of them sourced from a 375-wide phone capture, where an upscale invents pixels rather than recovers them. 660 is also the prose width the study already uses below 1024, so the walk stops introducing a sixth measure. THE 380 CAP IS NOT COSMETIC: Arrive and Post purchase are 375px captures, and at 536 the SMS thread rendered at 1.43x life size, at 660 it would be 1.76x - a phone screen shown bigger than a phone. THIS REPLACES THE 536 CAP AND THE ARGUMENT FOR IT, which reasoned about an asset set that no longer exists: under that set four of six crops were beneath their floor at full band width, which was true then and is not true now. Measured at the 660 cell: browse--page, browse--facet, pdp--page and cart--page 1.29x, options--wide 1.45x, cart--panel 1.27x. At the 380 cell: ad--post 1.32x, sms--standard 1.78x.
$cartDoc: PURCHASE IS A CONTEXT FRAME THEN A DETAIL FRAME, AND A SCROLL TRACK IS WHAT THAT REPLACED. cart--band.png was the full desktop cart at 2.06:1 and it was texture at a small cell, so an earlier build floored it at 1088 inside a focusable horizontal track and let it pan. That was measured and rejected: the banner cut mid-word, the nav truncated, and the location panel - the entire payload - sat off-frame, so the caption promised location and eligibility beside an image showing neither. cart--band.png was deleted on 31 Aug once nothing referenced it. The stage now runs cart--page for the whole page and cart--panel, cut from 08-cart-top_Upscale.png at 4090,640 1674x1480, for the panel itself: location, NOT ELIGIBLE FOR STORE PICKUP, free shipping, subtotal, checkout, every word legible. WHAT THE PANEL CROP GIVES UP IS THE TWO-DAY BANNER, which sits 3820px to its left across the top of the page - and the context frame above it is now where that banner is shown, which is the whole reason the two-frame rule exists.
$recutDoc: WHY FIVE ASSETS WERE RE-CUT ON 31 Aug AND THE ORIGINALS DELETED, so none of them is restored on the grounds that it exists in the history. pdp--standard opened on '$110.00' sliced through its own digits, with no product image, no product name and no breadcrumb - a column of form controls with no page around them. browse--feature began below the nav, the free-shipping banner and the page title, and ended mid product row. facet--detail was a heavy AI upscale with CORRUPTED LETTERFORMS: 'Delivery' and 'Free' with broken e's, 'Walnut Street' reading 'Stroet', a deformed ampersand - and on this site a screenshot with hallucinated glyphs is worse than a soft one, because it is WRONG rather than small. It was re-cut from 03-plp-filter-and-effect_Upscale.png, which nothing was using. ad--standard was cropped so tight it read as a display ad rather than as a feed post. cart--band is covered by $cartDoc.
$redactionDoc: ad--post.png CARRIES A VISIBLE REDACTION AND IT IS NOT TO BE CLEANED UP. One blurred region sits in the reaction row over the names of people who reacted to the post. They are real people, none of them Paul's, and the blur is visible ON PURPOSE: a visible redaction reads as care, where painting the names out in the background colour would be an undisclosed edit to a screenshot. This study refuses that everywhere else - it transcribes URBN's own 'No minumims' and 'There are no URBN location within 100 miles' exactly as they appear rather than correcting them - and the same principle governs here.
$homePageDoc: p16, THE HOME PAGE, IS STILL DELIBERATELY NOT CROPPED, AND BROWSE'S SECOND FRAME IS THE FACET DETAIL RATHER THAN THE HOME PAGE. Saying which asset fills that slot is the point of this entry: a later pass reading only 'the home page was cut' could restore it into a slot that is already filled. The reason it was cut stands - its promo tile repeats the social ad's free-2-day claim one step later in the same journey, and its store band repeats store--ribbon, so it would be more figures making claims the section already makes, which is the vocabulary problem the three-lens review found in section 03 wearing a new costume. Browse is carried by the PLP page and its facet close-up, which are a genuinely distinct capability.
